<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Item
1. Business</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>General
Background of the Company </B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Biomolecular
Life Holdings, Inc. (&ldquo;we&rdquo;, &ldquo;us&rdquo;, &ldquo;our&rdquo; or the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) traces its origins to Viral
Genetics, Inc., which was incorporated in the State of California on July 11, 1995. The Company&rsquo;s predecessor public company was
originally incorporated in the State of Delaware on June 8, 1998, as HITECH INVESTMENT, INC. On April 22, 1999, the Company changed
its name to 5 Star Living Online, Inc. On April 20, 2001, the Company entered into an agreement with Viral Genetics, Inc. (Viral), a
California corporation, concerning an anticipated merger and on November 5, 2001, the Company changed its name to Viral Genetics, Inc.
On November 26, 2012, the Company changed its name to VG Life Sciences, Inc. On January 27, 2023, the Company reincorporated in the State
of Florida. On May 27, 2025, the Board of Directors approved a change of the Company&rsquo;s name to SB Technology Holdings, Inc., which
was approved and became effective on April 16, 2026. On June 15, 2026, the Board of Directors approved a change of the Company&rsquo;s
name to Biomolecular Life Holdings, Inc., which was approved and became effective June 16, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><B>Recent Events</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Removal of Sole Officer
and Director</U></I>. On June 5, 2026, by written consent of the holder of a majority of the voting power of the Company&rsquo;s capital
stock, William P. Farrand was removed for cause as a director and as an officer of the Company, effective immediately. Following such
removal, Paul Strickland, the Company&rsquo;s Secretary, served as the sole director and sole officer of the Company until the change
of control described below.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 12pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Change in Control</U></I>.
On June 8, 2026, the Company entered into a Membership Interest Exchange and Change of Control Agreement (the &ldquo;Exchange Agreement&rdquo;)
and consummated the transactions contemplated thereby. Pursuant to the Exchange Agreement, the Company acquired one hundred percent (100%)
of the membership interests of Canvas 2709, LLC, a Florida limited liability company whose principal asset is real property located at
7311 NW 12th Street, Unit 15, Miami, Florida, and Selkirk Global Holdings, LLC transferred its 95,858,282 shares of Series A Preferred
Stock, representing voting control of the Company, to The David and Jessika Contreras Living Trust (the <B><I>&ldquo;Trust&rdquo;</I></B><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">).</FONT>
In connection with the closing, Paul Strickland resigned from all of his positions as a director and officer of the Company, and Jessika
Wiesner was appointed as the Company&rsquo;s sole director and as President, Chief Executive Officer, Secretary and Treasurer.
In connection with the foregoing, the Company changed its corporate name to Biomolecular Life Holdings, Inc. (See <I>Item 7. Certain
Relationships and Related Transactions</I>).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Marketing Services and
License Agreement</U></I>. On July 23, 2026, the Company entered into a Marketing Services and License Agreement (the &ldquo;Marketing
Agreement&rdquo;) with Biomolecular Life LLC, a Florida limited liability company (&ldquo;BML&rdquo;). BML develops, markets, and sells
a line of dietary supplement products for humans and pets under the &ldquo;Biomolecular Life&rdquo; brand, including its BIOREVIT (vitality
and energy support), IMMUNO (immune system support), and MEN (active men revitalization) products, together with such additional products
as the parties may add by mutual written agreement (collectively, the &ldquo;Products&rdquo;).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Jessika Wiesner, the Company&rsquo;s
sole director and its President, Chief Executive Officer, Secretary and Treasurer, is the manager of BML and executed the Marketing Agreement
on behalf of both parties. The Marketing Agreement is, therefore, a related-party transaction and was approved by written consent of
the Company&rsquo;s Board of Directors and by written consent of the manager of BML, in each case following full disclosure of that common
service and interest and in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Florida Statutes, respectively. (See <I>Item 1A. Risk Factors</I>
and <I>Item 7. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions</I>). The Marketing Agreement was not negotiated at arm&rsquo;s length
and its terms may be less favorable to the Company than terms the Company could have obtained from an unaffiliated party.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I>Appointment and Services</I>.
BML has appointed the Company as BML&rsquo;s exclusive provider of advertising, marketing, and promotion management services for the
Products during the term. The Company is responsible for developing and executing the advertising and marketing strategy for the Products;
planning, managing, and placing advertising; managing social media, digital marketing, and email marketing campaigns; developing marketing
content and creative materials, subject to BML&rsquo;s approval; managing promotional partnerships and affiliate and influencer programs;
brand management for the Products; and providing marketing analytics and periodic reporting to BML.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I>License</I>. BML has granted
the Company a non-exclusive, royalty-free license during the term to use BML&rsquo;s trademarks, service marks, trade names, trade dress,
logos, and brand elements, including the name &ldquo;Biomolecular Life&rdquo; and the Product names, for all branding, marketing, advertising,
and promotional purposes in connection with the Products and the parties&rsquo; business. The license is not limited to the performance
of the services, and the Company may sublicense the marks to its contractors and service providers as reasonably necessary for those
purposes. The marks are and remain the exclusive property of BML, all goodwill arising from the Company&rsquo;s use inures solely to
BML, and the license terminates upon termination of the Marketing Agreement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I>Compensation</I>. BML will
pay the Company a marketing fee equal to fifteen percent (15%) of Net Revenue during the term (the &ldquo;Marketing Fee&rdquo;). &ldquo;Net
Revenue&rdquo; means the gross amounts actually received by BML from sales of the Products during the applicable period, less (i) returns,
refunds, and chargebacks; (ii) discounts, rebates, and allowances actually granted; (iii) sales, use, excise, value-added, and similar
taxes collected from customers; and (iv) shipping and handling charges collected from customers and passed through to third parties.
Within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter, BML must deliver to the Company a written report calculating Net Revenue
for that quarter and pay the Marketing Fee then due. BML must maintain books and records sufficient to verify Net Revenue for at least
three (3) years, and the Company may review those records not more than once in any twelve (12) month period, at the Company&rsquo;s
expense, solely to verify the Marketing Fee.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>Third-Party
Costs</I>. All third-party media, advertising, and promotional spend is subject to a budget approved in advance in writing by BML, and
approved third-party costs are paid or reimbursed by BML. The Company bears its own internal personnel and overhead costs.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>Allocation
of Responsibility</I>. As between the parties, BML remains solely responsible for the formulation, manufacture, labeling, packaging,
pricing, sale, fulfillment, and customer service of the Products and for the substantiation of all claims made with respect to the Products,
and has final approval over all marketing materials prior to their public use. The Company has no authority to execute contracts or make
commitments on behalf of BML except as expressly authorized by BML in writing. The Company is an independent contractor of BML.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>Term
and Termination</I>. The Marketing Agreement commenced on August 7, 2026, and continues for an initial term of one (1) year, automatically
renewing for successive one (1) year terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the
end of the then-current term. Either party may terminate the Marketing Agreement at any time upon thirty (30) days&rsquo; prior written
notice, and either party may terminate immediately upon an uncured material breach or upon specified insolvency events. The Marketing
Agreement terminates automatically, without further action of the parties, upon the closing of any merger, acquisition, share exchange,
or other business combination between the parties or their respective affiliates, unless the parties otherwise agree in writing.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>Compliance;
Other Terms</I>. Each party has covenanted to comply with all laws applicable to its performance, including the Federal Food, Drug, and
Cosmetic Act, the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act of 1994, the Federal Trade Commission Act and the FTC&rsquo;s advertising,
endorsement, and testimonial guides, the CAN-SPAM Act, the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, and applicable state consumer protection
laws. The Company may not make, or cause to be made, any claim regarding the Products that has not been approved by BML, and neither
party may represent that the Products diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease. The Marketing Agreement also contains customary
confidentiality, indemnification, and limitation of liability provisions; the Company&rsquo;s aggregate liability is capped at the Marketing
Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, subject to exceptions for the confidentiality
and indemnification provisions. Disputes are subject to binding arbitration in Miami-Dade County, Florida, and the Marketing Agreement
is governed by Florida law.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
foregoing description of the Marketing Agreement is not complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the
Marketing Agreement, a copy of which is filed as Exhibit 10.7 to this Registration Statement and is incorporated herein by reference.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Exit
from Shell Status</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Prior
to July 23, 2026, the Company was a &ldquo;shell&rdquo; company, as that term is defined in Rule 405 under the Securities Act and Rule
12b-2 under the Exchange Act, whose purpose was to locate and consummate a merger or acquisition with a private entity. On July 23, 2026,
the Company entered into the Marketing Agreement described above and commenced the operations described below under &ldquo;Plan of Business.&rdquo;
The Company believes that, as a result, it is no longer a shell company,</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Plan
of Business</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
execution of the Marketing Agreement, the Company ceased to be an entity whose sole purpose was to locate and consummate a business combination
and commenced operations as a provider of marketing, advertising, and brand management services to companies in the dietary supplement
and consumer wellness sector. The Company&rsquo;s plan of business is set forth below. The plan is forward-looking, requires capital
the Company does not presently have, and is subject to the risks described in Item 1A, &ldquo;Risk Factors,&rdquo; including the Company&rsquo;s
current dependence on a single related-party client and the ability of either party to terminate the Marketing Agreement on thirty (30)
days&rsquo; notice. No assurance can be given that the Company will implement any portion of this plan.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Commercial
Status of the Products. BML commercially launched the BIOREVIT, IMMUNO and MEN products in January 2026 and BML has generated aggregate
gross sales of the Products of approximately $100,000 through June 30, 2026. Since entering into the Marketing Agreement in July 2026,
the Company has earned approximately $5,000 in Marketing Fees.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company does not manufacture, own, price, sell or fulfill the Products and has no control over whether or when BML continues to sell
any Product. BML may discontinue any Product at any time, and either party may terminate the Marketing Agreement on thirty (30) days&rsquo;
notice.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 5; Value: 2 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><TD STYLE="text-align: center; width: 100%"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->5<!-- Field: /Sequence --></TD></TR></TABLE></DIV>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Phase One &mdash; Establish
the marketing operation (months 1 through 6). During the first six months, the Company intends to: (i) engage a marketing director and
creative, media-buying, and analytics personnel on a contract, part-time, or full-time basis as capital permits; (ii) implement a marketing
technology stack, including web and commerce analytics, an email service provider, social media scheduling and listening tools, and affiliate
and influencer tracking; (iii) complete a brand audit of the Products and adopt written brand guidelines with BML as contemplated by
the quality control provisions of the Marketing Agreement; (iv) adopt a written advertising compliance program, including a documented
claim-review and approval workflow with BML, covering structure/function claims under the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act
of 1994, substantiation requirements and the FTC&rsquo;s endorsement and testimonial guides, and CAN-SPAM and Telephone Consumer Protection
Act compliance; (v) agree the first annual third-party media budget with BML; (vi) launch paid search, paid social, email, and affiliate
campaigns for the BIOREVIT, IMMUNO, and MEN products; and (vii) implement quarterly procedures to receive, test, and reconcile BML&rsquo;s
Net Revenue reports and the resulting Marketing Fee.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Phase Two &mdash; Reduce client
concentration (months 6 through 18). The Company&rsquo;s revenue is presently derived entirely from a single related-party client. The
Company&rsquo;s principal objective in the second phase is to reduce that concentration by marketing its services to unaffiliated brands.
The Company intends to: (i) develop a standardized service offering and rate card, including percentage-of-revenue, monthly retainer,
and fixed-fee project structures, so that the Company is not dependent on a revenue-share model that pays only if a client sells; (ii)
solicit unaffiliated dietary supplement, pet wellness, functional food, and consumer health brands, with the stated objective that unaffiliated
clients generate a majority of the Company&rsquo;s revenue by the end of the phase; (iii) build a network of contract creative, media,
and production vendors; (iv) develop case studies and performance data from the Product campaigns, subject to the confidentiality provisions
of the Marketing Agreement; and (v) evaluate the addition of adjacent services, including fulfillment-adjacent marketing operations,
subscription and retention program management, and marketplace channel management.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Phase Three &mdash; Owned
brands and scale (months 18 through 36). In the third phase, the Company intends to evaluate transitioning from a services-only model,
in which it markets brands owned by others, to a model in which it also owns brands and the associated intellectual property and revenue.
Alternatives under consideration include the acquisition or in-licensing of one or more consumer wellness brands, the development of
Company-owned brands, and a business combination with BML or another operating company. Any such transaction would require capital the
Company does not presently have and, in the case of a business combination with BML or its affiliates, would cause the Marketing Agreement
to terminate automatically by its terms. The Company has not entered into any agreement, arrangement, or understanding with respect to
any such transaction.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Revenue Model</U></I>.
The Company&rsquo;s only contracted revenue source is the Marketing Fee, equal to 15% of BML&rsquo;s Net Revenue from the Products. The
Company therefore earns revenue only to the extent BML actually sells Products and actually collects the sales price, and the Company
does not control BML&rsquo;s formulation, pricing, inventory, fulfillment, or customer service, each of which BML retains under the Marketing
Agreement. Because approved third-party media spend is paid or reimbursed by BML while the Company bears its own personnel and overhead,
the Company&rsquo;s margin is a function of its own cost structure rather than of media cost, but the Company will incur those personnel
and overhead costs before, and regardless of whether, any Marketing Fee is earned.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Personnel and Facilities</U></I>.
As of the date of this Registration Statement, the Company has one part-time employee, who is also its sole officer and director. The
Company intends to add marketing personnel on a contract or part-time basis as capital permits and does not expect to add full-time employees
until unaffiliated client revenue supports the cost. The Company does not require, and does not intend to acquire, dedicated laboratory,
manufacturing, or fulfillment facilities, because BML retains responsibility for those functions under the Marketing Agreement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Capital Requirements
and Milestones</U></I>. The Company estimates that implementing Phase One will require additional capital, the amount of which will depend
on the personnel and technology commitments the Company elects to make and on the timing of Marketing Fee receipts. The Company does
not currently have sufficient working capital to fund its operations over the next twelve months and expects to fund the plan through
a combination of Marketing Fee revenue, loans from affiliates, and future issuances of debt or equity securities, which would be dilutive
to existing holders. The Company has no commitment from any person to provide such capital. The principal milestones by which management
intends to measure progress are the adoption of the compliance program and brand guidelines, the first full quarter of Marketing Fee
revenue, the engagement of the first unaffiliated client, and the point at which unaffiliated clients account for a majority of revenue.
(See <I>Item 2. Financial Information &mdash; Management&rsquo;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
&mdash; Liquidity and Capital Resources</I>).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><B>Competition</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Following the execution of
the Marketing Agreement, we face competition on two distinct levels. We compete directly for engagements to provide marketing, advertising,
and brand management services. We are also exposed indirectly to the competition our client faces in selling the Products, because our
Marketing Fee is calculated as a percentage of BML&rsquo;s Net Revenue and we therefore earn revenue only to the extent the Products
compete successfully. We have not commissioned or obtained any third-party market study, and the following discussion reflects management&rsquo;s
assessment rather than independent research.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Competition for Our
Services</U></I>. The market for marketing, advertising, and brand management services is intensely competitive, highly fragmented, and
characterized by very low barriers to entry. We compete, or expect to compete, with:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; global advertising
and marketing holding companies and their digital, media-buying, and performance marketing units;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; independent digital
and performance marketing agencies, including agencies specializing in direct-to-consumer and subscription commerce;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; specialist agencies
focused on dietary supplements, nutrition, and consumer wellness, which possess category experience and regulatory familiarity that we
have not yet demonstrated;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; individual consultants,
freelancers, and contractors engaged directly or through online talent marketplaces, which compete principally on price;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; influencer and affiliate
marketing networks and software platforms that permit a brand to operate such programs without engaging an agency; and</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; the self-service advertising,
analytics, and retail media tools offered by the major advertising platforms and online marketplaces, which permit a brand to plan, place,
and measure advertising without any intermediary.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The most significant competitor
of any provider of marketing services is the prospective client&rsquo;s own in-house marketing function. Many consumer brands perform
some or all of these functions internally, and a prospective client&rsquo;s decision to build an internal capability rather than engage
a third party would eliminate the opportunity entirely.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Competition in our market
is principally on the basis of demonstrated performance, category and regulatory expertise, price and fee structure, breadth of services
offered, the experience of assigned personnel, and existing relationships. We have no operating history in this business, no completed
client engagement other than our engagement by BML, and no performance record that we are presently able to present to a prospective
client. Substantially all of our competitors have greater financial, personnel, technical, and creative resources than we do, together
with longer operating histories, established client relationships, and existing case studies. We expect to be at a significant competitive
disadvantage in competing for unaffiliated clients until we have developed a demonstrable performance record.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Competition Affecting
the Products</U></I>. Because our Marketing Fee is a percentage of BML&rsquo;s Net Revenue, we bear indirect exposure to competitive
conditions in the dietary supplement market even though we do not formulate, manufacture, price, sell, or fulfill any product. That market
is large, highly fragmented, and intensely competitive. The Products compete with:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; diversified manufacturers
with national retail distribution, mass and club channel shelf space, and substantial advertising budgets;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; direct-to-consumer
and subscription supplement brands, many of which are venture-funded and compete aggressively for customer acquisition;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; private label and
retailer-owned brands, which typically compete on price; and</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; a large number of
small sellers offering competing products through online marketplaces.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 7; Value: 2 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><TD STYLE="text-align: center; width: 100%"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->7<!-- Field: /Sequence --></TD></TR></TABLE></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Barriers to entry in the dietary
supplement category are low. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration does not approve dietary supplements before they are marketed, and
a firm is not required to provide the FDA with the evidence on which it relies to substantiate safety before or after it markets a product,
except in the case of certain new dietary ingredients. The manufacturer or distributor bears the initial responsibility for ensuring
that its products meet applicable safety standards and must have substantiation that any structure/function claim it makes is truthful
and not misleading. The practical effect of this regulatory structure is that competing products can be brought to market quickly and
at low cost, which increases the number of products competing for the same consumers and for the same advertising inventory, and which
raises the cost of the advertising we will purchase on BML&rsquo;s behalf.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">We do not control any of the
factors that determine whether the Products compete successfully. Under the Marketing Agreement, BML retains sole responsibility for
the formulation, manufacture, labeling, packaging, pricing, sale, fulfillment, and customer service of the Products, and has final approval
over all marketing materials before their public use. A competitive development that reduces BML&rsquo;s Net Revenue will reduce our
Marketing Fee, and we would have no contractual remedy.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><I><U>Our Competitive Position</U></I>.
We are a new entrant with one client, one part-time executive officer, no employees dedicated to performing the services, no revenue
to date under the Marketing Agreement, and limited capital. We own no brand, no product, no proprietary technology, and no patent, and
the marks we use are licensed to us on a non-exclusive basis and revert to BML upon termination of the Marketing Agreement. We regard
these as material competitive disadvantages, and we do not believe that we presently compete effectively for unaffiliated business.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">We believe the following are
the principal factors that may permit us to compete over time, although we can give no assurance that any of them will prove sufficient:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; our exclusive appointment
as BML&rsquo;s provider of the Services for the Products, which gives us a live account against which to build capability and, subject
to BML&rsquo;s consent under the confidentiality provisions of the Marketing Agreement, a performance record;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; the breadth of the
license granted to us, which is not limited to the performance of the Services and permits us to sublicense the marks to our contractors
and service providers, allowing us to add capacity without adding fixed personnel cost;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; the allocation to
BML of approved third-party media and promotional spend, which means we are not required to fund media purchases out of our own working
capital; and</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&#9679; our status as a reporting
company under the Exchange Act, which may improve our access to capital and afford a level of public disclosure that some prospective
clients regard favorably.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Each of these factors is contingent.
The exclusive appointment, the license, and the allocation of media cost all arise from a single agreement with a related party that
either party may terminate on thirty (30) days&rsquo; notice, and none of them survives its termination. (See <I>Item 1A. Risk Factors
&mdash; Risks Related to the Marketing Agreement and Our Operating Business</I>).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

active trading market commences, there can be no assurance as to the market price of our common stock, whether the trading market will
provide liquidity to investors or whether any trading market will be sustained.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Employees</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Conflicts
of Interest <I></I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">There exist potential
conflicts of interest between our Sole Officer and Director, Jessika Wiesner, inasmuch as BML, the company with which the Company
entered into the Marketing Agreement, is owned by Ms. Wiesner and upon which the Company is dependent for generating revenues.
Ms. Wiesner intends to resolve any such conflicts of interest in accordance with her fiduciary duties owed to the Company.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I></I></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Certain
Regulatory Matters</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company is an &ldquo;emerging growth company,&rdquo; as defined in Section 2(a) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &ldquo;Securities
Act&rdquo;), as modified by the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of 2012 (the &ldquo;JOBS Act&rdquo;). As such, the Company is eligible
to take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting requirements that are applicable to other public companies that are not
emerging growth companies including, but not limited to, not being required to comply with the independent registered public accounting
firm attestation requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (the &ldquo;Sarbanes-Oxley Act&rdquo;), reduced disclosure
obligations regarding executive compensation in our periodic reports and proxy statements, and exemptions from the requirements of holding
a non-binding advisory vote on executive compensation and stockholder approval of any golden parachute payments not previously approved.
If some investors find our securities less attractive as a result, there may be a less active trading market for our securities and the
prices of our securities may be more volatile.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
addition, Section 107 of the JOBS Act also provides that an emerging growth company can take advantage of the extended transition period
provided in Section 7(a)(2)(B) of the Securities Act for complying with new or revised accounting standards. In other words, an emerging
growth company can delay the adoption of certain accounting standards until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies.
We intend to take advantage of the benefits of this extended transition period.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company will remain an emerging growth company until the earlier of (1) the last day of the fiscal year (a) following the fifth anniversary
of the Company&rsquo;s first public offering of its securities, (b) in which the Company has total annual gross revenue of at least $1.235
billion, or (c) in which the Company is deemed to be a large accelerated filer, which means the market value of the Company&rsquo;s common
stock that is held by non-affiliates exceeds $700 million as of the prior June 30, and (2) the date on which the Company has issued more
than $1.0 billion in non-convertible debt securities during the prior three-year period. References herein to emerging growth company
will have the meaning associated with it in the JOBS Act.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Additionally,
the Company is a &ldquo;smaller reporting company&rdquo; as defined in Item 10(f)(1) of Regulation S-K. Smaller reporting companies
may take advantage of certain reduced disclosure obligations, including, among other things, providing only two years of audited financial
statements. The Company will remain a smaller reporting company until the last day of the fiscal year in which (1) the market value of
the Company&rsquo;s common stock held by non-affiliates exceeds $250 million as of the end of the prior June 30th, or (2) the Company&rsquo;s
annual revenues exceeded $100 million during such completed fiscal year and the market value of the Company&rsquo;s common stock held
by non-affiliates exceeds $700 million as of the prior June 30th.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Item
1A: Risk Factors</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>RISK
FACTORS </B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>The
statements contained in this Form 10 that are not historic facts are forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties
that could cause actual results to differ materially from those set forth in or implied by forward-looking statements. If any of the
following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects could be harmed.</I></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -10pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Risks
Related to The Company</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
auditors have expressed substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern. </I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
audited financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, were prepared using the assumption that we will continue
our operations as a going concern. Our independent accountants in their audit report have expressed substantial doubt about our ability
to continue as a going concern. Our ability to continue as a going concern is dependent on our ability to raise sufficient capital
and to generate revenue under the Marketing Agreement and from additional clients. Our financial statements do not include any adjustments
that may result from the outcome of this uncertainty. Although we have some cash on hand, there is not enough cash on hand to fund our
administrative expenses and operating expenses for the next twelve months. Therefore, we may be unable to continue operations in the
future as a going concern. If we cannot continue as a viable entity, our stockholders may lose some or all of their investment in the
Company&rsquo;s shares of common stock.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
owe $400,000 to our control party under a note that matures on October 6, 2027, we cannot prepay it without the holder&rsquo;s consent,
and we have no committed source of funds with which to repay it.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
October 7, 2026, we issued to The David and Jessika Contreras Living Trust (the Trust) a convertible promissory note in the principal
amount of $400,000 (the <B><I>&ldquo;Note&rdquo;</I></B>) and a five-year warrant to purchase 400,000 shares of our common stock (the
<B><I>&ldquo;Warrant&rdquo;</I></B>), for aggregate cash proceeds of $400,000. The Note matures on October 6, 2027, bears interest at
6% per annum and is payable in a single payment of principal and accrued interest at maturity. We may not prepay the Note, in whole or
in part, without the Trust&rsquo;s prior written consent, and we cannot compel the Trust to convert it. We have no committed source of
funds with which to repay the Note, we have no operating history of generating cash from operations in our current business, and we may
be unable to refinance the Note on acceptable terms or at all.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
an event of default, the entire outstanding balance may be declared immediately due and payable and interest accrues at 12% per annum.
The events of default include, in addition to a failure to pay, our failure to use commercially reasonable efforts to file our Exchange
Act reports on a timely basis or, if we are not then subject to those requirements, to make publicly available the information required
by Rule 15c2-11. Accordingly, a failure to satisfy our reporting obligations would not only affect the eligibility of our common stock
for quotation but would also permit the Trust to accelerate the Note. The Note is held by the party that controls our company and whose
trustee is our sole director; the decision whether to declare a default, to accelerate, to grant a waiver or to convert rests entirely
with that party.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>The
Note and the Warrant were not negotiated at arm&rsquo;s length, and our sole director and officer executed them on behalf of both parties.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Jessika
Wiesner, our sole director and our President, Chief Executive Officer, Secretary and Treasurer, is the trustee of the Trust and
executed the Note and the Warrant on behalf of both the Company and the Trust. No independent
director, independent committee or financial advisor reviewed the transaction, and no fairness determination was obtained. The
interest rate, the $1.00 conversion price, the $3.00 warrant exercise price, the 100% warrant coverage, the prohibition on
prepayment without the holder&rsquo;s consent and the events of default may each be less favorable to us than terms we could have
obtained from an unaffiliated lender. We expect that any future financing provided by the Trust will present the same
conflict.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>The
Company has a limited operating history and limited resources. </I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company has only recently emerged from &ldquo;shell company&rdquo; status and has no history of operations in the marketing services
business. Currently, the Company has limited capital resources with which to generate revenues and there is no assurance that the
Company will be able to obtain adequate capital with which to operate.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>The
Company is dependent on its key personnel, the loss of which would impair the Company&rsquo;s ability to perform its obligations under
the Marketing Agreement and to implement its Plan of Business. </I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
performing its obligations under the Marketing Agreement and implementing its Plan of Business, the Company is dependent upon the continued
services of management,</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"> particularly Jessika Wiesner,
the Company&rsquo;s President, Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, Treasurer and sole director. To the extent that the services of such
persons become unavailable, the Company will be required to obtain other qualified personnel and there can be no assurance that we will
be able to recruit one or more qualified persons upon acceptable terms.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>The
Company&rsquo;s executive officers and directors may allocate their time to other businesses activities, thereby causing conflicts of
interest as to how much time to devote to the Company&rsquo;s affairs. This could have a negative impact on the Company&rsquo;s ability
to perform the Services and to implement its Plan of Business. </I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s executive officers and directors are not required and do not commit their full time to the Company&rsquo;s affairs, which
may result in a conflict of interest in allocating their time between the Company&rsquo;s business and other businesses. The Company
has no full-time employees and does not expect to engage dedicated marketing personnel until it obtains additional capital. Our executive
officers and directors are engaged in other business endeavors and they are not obligated to contribute any specific number of hours
per week to the Company&rsquo;s affairs.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If
the other business affairs of our executive officers and directors require them to devote more time to such affairs, it could limit their
ability to devote time to the Company&rsquo;s affairs, which could have a negative impact on the Company&rsquo;s ability to perform
the Services and to implement its Plan of Business. Furthermore, we do not have an employment agreement with any of our executive
officers or directors.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>The
holder of our Series A Preferred Stock controls the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our shareholders, and control of our
company may be transferred without any conversion of the Series A Preferred Stock into common stock.</I></B></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>
</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">All
95,858,282 outstanding shares of our Series A Preferred Stock are held of record by The David and Jessika Contreras Living Trust (the
&ldquo;Trust&rdquo;), the trustee of which is Jessika Wiesner, our sole director and our President, Chief Executive Officer, Secretary
and Treasurer. Each share of Series A Preferred Stock carries 10,000 votes on all matters submitted to a vote of our shareholders, and
the Series A Preferred Stock votes together with our common stock. The Trust therefore controls 958,582,820,000 votes, or approximately
99.99% of our total voting power, as against the 68,196,265 votes represented by all of our outstanding shares of common stock.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
a result, Ms. Wiesner, acting as trustee of the Trust, has the voting power to determine the outcome of every matter presented
to the holders of our common stock for a vote, including the election of all of our directors, any amendment to our articles of incorporation
or our bylaws, and the approval of any major corporate transaction, including a change in control, a merger, a consolidation or a sale
of all or substantially all of our assets. The holders of our common stock cannot, acting alone or together, determine the outcome of
any such matter, and their votes will not affect the outcome of any matter for so long as the Trust holds a majority of our voting power.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Because
of the 10,000-to-one voting ratio, the Trust would be required to retain only a very small number of shares of Series A Preferred Stock
in order to maintain voting control. Based on 68,196,265 shares of common stock outstanding as of the date of this Registration Statement,
the holder of 5,107 shares of Series A Preferred Stock would control 51,070,000 votes, which is a majority of our combined voting power.
The Trust could therefore sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of as many as 95,853,175 shares of Series A Preferred Stock, more than
99.99% of the outstanding Series A Preferred Stock, and still control the outcome of every matter submitted to a vote of our shareholders.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Control
of our company can be transferred without any conversion of the Series A Preferred Stock into common stock. The Series A Preferred Stock
is convertible only at the option of the holder. Neither our articles of incorporation nor the designation of the Series A Preferred
Stock requires conversion of those shares upon a transfer of the shares, upon the death of a holder, upon an intra-family transfer, or
upon any other event, and there is no sunset provision that terminates the super-voting rights after any period of time. Ms. Wiesner
may therefore transfer voting control of our company either by causing the Trust to transfer shares of Series A Preferred Stock to a
third party, or, because the shares are held in a trust, by transferring control of the Trust itself, for example by resigning as trustee
and appointing a successor trustee, by amending or revoking the Trust, or by transferring the beneficial interests in the Trust. A transfer
of control of the Trust would not be a transfer of the Series A Preferred Stock, would not cause those shares to convert into common
stock, and could occur without any vote of, notice to, consent from, or payment to the holders of our common stock.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Holding
the Series A Preferred Stock in a trust affords greater flexibility with respect to transfers of beneficial ownership than direct ownership
by an individual would. Beneficial ownership of the Series A Preferred Stock may be shifted among the beneficiaries of the Trust, and
the terms of the Trust may be amended, without any transfer of record ownership of the shares and without conversion of the shares into
common stock. A change in the beneficial ownership of our controlling security effected in that manner may not be promptly apparent from
our public filings, and holders of our common stock may have no advance notice that control of our company has changed hands.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
Series A Preferred Stock has anti-takeover effects that could prevent a change in control transaction that holders of our common stock
might consider to be in their best interests, and future issuances of Series A Preferred Stock would be dilutive to holders of our common
stock.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
super-voting rights of the Series A Preferred Stock have anti-takeover effects. Because the Trust controls approximately 99.99% of our
voting power, no person can acquire control of our company through the accumulation of common stock, through a proxy contest or through
a tender offer without the consent of the Trust. The Trust may decline to approve, or may use its voting power to defeat, a merger, tender
offer, sale of assets or other change in control transaction that the holders of our common stock believe to be in their best interests,
including a transaction that would afford them a premium over the then-current market price of our common stock. The Series A Preferred
Stock also carries an aggregate $4,000,000 liquidation preference payable ahead of any distribution to the holders of our common stock
upon a sale of the Company or of all or substantially all of its assets, a dividend preference of twice the amount paid on the common
stock, and a right of first refusal to participate in or purchase stock in any registration statement we file. Each of these features
may further deter a third party from proposing a transaction with us.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Future
issuances of Series A Preferred Stock would be dilutive to the holders of our common stock. We are authorized to issue 100,000,000 shares
of Series A Preferred Stock, of which 95,858,282 shares are outstanding and 4,141,718 shares remain available for issuance. Our board
of directors, which consists solely of Ms. Wiesner, may issue those remaining shares at any time, for such consideration as it
determines, without the approval of the holders of our common stock. Because each share of Series A Preferred Stock carries 10,000 votes
and is convertible into one share of common stock, an issuance of additional shares would dilute the voting power of our common stock
out of all proportion to the economic interest those shares represent. The issuance of all 4,141,718 remaining authorized shares would
create 41,417,180,000 additional votes. Any such issuance could be used to entrench our management or to defeat a change in control transaction
and would further dilute the voting power and, upon conversion, the economic interest of the holders of our common stock.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I></I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
incur significant costs as a reporting company, and our reporting obligations could delay or preclude a future acquisition.</I></B></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Sections
13 and 15(d) of the Exchange Act require companies subject thereto to provide certain information about significant acquisitions, including
certified financial statements for the company acquired, covering one, two, or three years, depending on the relative size of the acquisition.
The time and additional costs that may be incurred by some target entities to prepare such statements may significantly delay or essentially
preclude consummation of an otherwise desirable acquisition by the Company. Acquisition prospects that do not have or are unable to obtain
the required audited statements may not be appropriate for acquisition so long as the reporting requirements of the Exchange Act are

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company will continue to be required to file quarterly reports on Form 10-Q and annual reports on Form 10-K, which annual report must
contain the Company&rsquo;s audited financial statements. The Company is not a blank check company and does not have as its business
plan the acquisition of an unidentified business; however, management has identified a possible business combination as one alternative
under &ldquo;Plan of Business &mdash; Phase Three,&rdquo; and the following would apply to any such transaction. As a reporting
company under the Exchange Act, following any business combination, we will be required to file a report on Form 8-K (a so-called &ldquo;Super
8-K&rsquo; wherein we provide &ldquo;Form 10 information&rdquo;). Audited financial statements must be filed with the SEC within five
(5) days following the closing of a business combination. While obtaining audited financial statements is typically the responsibility
of the acquired company, it is possible that a potential target company may be a non-reporting company with unaudited financial statements.
The time and costs that may be incurred by some potential target companies to prepare such audited financial statements may significantly
delay or may even preclude consummation of an otherwise desirable business combination. Acquisition prospects that do not have or are
unable to obtain the required audited statements may not be appropriate for acquisition because we are subject to the reporting requirements
of the Exchange Act.</FONT></P>
